config.title: useToggle

intro.title: useToggle
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom Angular hook called 'useToggle' to manage a boolean state that can be switched between true and false. You will learn how to encapsulate state logic into a reusable function using Angular's built-in APIs like useState and useCallback. The main technologies involved are Angular hooks, TypeScript for type safety, and functional components. By the end, you'll understand how to create and use custom hooks to simplify state management in your Angular applications.
intro.usecase: The useToggle pattern is fundamental for managing binary UI states in real applications. You'll use it to control visibility of modals, expand/collapse panels in dashboards, toggle between light/dark themes, and switch form fields between edit/view modes. In e-commerce sites, it powers product filter toggles (like 'In Stock Only'), while in admin panels it controls sidebar menus and detail view expansions. Every interactive element with an on/off, show/hide, or expand/collapse behavior relies on this toggle logic.

objectives: Implement a custom useToggle hook in an Angular component
Initialize a boolean state variable with a default value using the useToggle hook
Bind the toggle state to UI elements to control their visibility
Manipulate the toggle state by triggering event handlers
Integrate the toggle functionality with multiple UI components
Configure the toggle to accept and use an initial state parameter
Apply the useToggle hook to create interactive user interface elements

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core
steps.instruction: In your TypeScript file, import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import keyword followed by the symbol name and the module path in quotes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular imports are added to the file, enabling component creation and basic template directives.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Component and CommonModule from their correct Angular packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the ToggleComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the ToggleComponent class with the @Component decorator below the imports. Set the selector to 'app-toggle' and the template to a simple heading for now.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define the component metadata, then create an empty class named ToggleComponent.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Define the ToggleComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A ToggleComponent class is defined with @Component decorator configured with selector 'app-toggle' and a basic template.
successCriteria: ToggleComponent class exists with @Component decorator having selector 'app-toggle' and template containing a heading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you have both the @Component decorator with selector 'app-toggle' and the ToggleComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure isn't complete. Check that you have the @Component decorator and ToggleComponent class defined.

steps.title: Initialize the toggle state property
steps.instruction: Inside the ToggleComponent class, add a public boolean property called 'isOn' to track the toggle state, initializing it to false.
steps.hint: Add a property declaration with type annotation and initial value in the component class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ToggleComponent class will have a typed boolean property to track toggle state.
successCriteria: The component has a public property named 'isOn' of type boolean initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure 'isOn' is a public boolean property initialized to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component needs a boolean property to track toggle state. Try adding 'public isOn: boolean = false' inside the class.

steps.title: Define the toggle handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the ToggleComponent class, add a method named toggle that flips the value of the isOn property between true and false.
steps.hint: You can toggle a boolean value using the logical NOT operator (!).
steps.expectedOutcome: The ToggleComponent class now has a toggle method that can be called to change the isOn state.
successCriteria: The toggle method is defined in the ToggleComponent class and correctly toggles the isOn property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your toggle method uses the logical NOT operator (!) to flip the isOn value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle method isn't defined correctly. Remember to create a method that changes isOn to the opposite boolean value.

steps.title: Set up the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a div container with class 'toggle-container' to the component's template.
steps.hint: Place the div inside the template string of the @Component decorator.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now has a div container with the class 'toggle-container'.
successCriteria: The template string contains a div element with class='toggle-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but make sure it has the class 'toggle-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template should contain a div with class='toggle-container'.

steps.title: Display the current toggle state
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a paragraph element that displays the current value of the 'isOn' property using Angular interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to interpolate the 'isOn' property value directly in the template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying a property value

Current status: {{ isActive }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show a paragraph that displays 'false' initially and updates to 'true' when the toggle is clicked.
successCriteria: A paragraph element is added to the template that uses interpolation to display the value of the 'isOn' property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a paragraph element with interpolation syntax ({{ }}) that references the 'isOn' property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the toggle state. Add a paragraph element using Angular interpolation to show the value of 'isOn'.

steps.title: Add the toggle button element
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text 'Toggle' to your component's template.
steps.hint: In Angular templates, you can add a button using the <button> HTML element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button in an Angular template
<button>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template now contains a button element with the text 'Toggle'.
successCriteria: A <button>Toggle</button> element is present in the component's template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the toggle button to the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a button element with the exact text 'Toggle'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is missing or incorrect. Add a <button>Toggle</button> to the template.

steps.title: Wire the button click to the toggle handler
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a (click) event binding to the button element that calls the toggle() method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax: (event)="handler()". For click events, use (click)="toggle()" on the button element.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: wiring a button click to a method
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will now respond to clicks and trigger the toggle logic when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element has a (click) event binding that calls the toggle() method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using Angular's event binding syntax (click)="toggle()" on the button element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button click isn't properly wired to the toggle handler. Remember to use (click)="toggle()" on the button element.

steps.title: Add conditional styling based on toggle state
steps.instruction: Add a class binding to the button element to apply the 'active' CSS class when the toggle state is true. Use Angular's property binding syntax with [class.className].
steps.hint: Use [class.active]="isOn" to conditionally add the 'active' class when isOn is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button element will have dynamic styling that changes based on the toggle state.
successCriteria: The button element includes [class.active] binding with the isOn property as the condition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the correct property binding syntax for class binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button doesn't have the conditional class binding. Try using [class.active]="isOn" on the button element.

steps.title: Add descriptive text based on toggle state
steps.instruction: In the component template, add a <span> element that displays 'ON' when isOn is true and 'OFF' when isOn is false using a ternary expression.
steps.analogousExample: // Conditional text display in Angular template {{ isActive ? 'Active' : 'Inactive' }}
steps.expectedOutcome: A span element showing 'ON' or 'OFF' based on the toggle state appears below the button.
successCriteria: The template contains a <span> element with a ternary expression {{ isOn ? 'ON' : 'OFF' }}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using a ternary expression inside {{ }} to display 'ON' or 'OFF' based on isOn.
steps.feedbackWrong: The span element with conditional text isn't implemented correctly. Review how to use ternary expressions in Angular templates.
